tossups.text: this structure is essential for alveoli structure and function. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in alveoli structure and function.

tossups.text: This mythical resident of Lemnos was born parthenogenetically, and built a trick throne to ensnare his mother. This figure created the first woman, Pandora, and split Zeus's head open to release Athena. This god created a fine net to trap Ares and this god's wife, Aphrodite, in his lair beneath a volcano. For 10 points, name this son of Hera, the deformed Greek god of fire and patron of smiths.

The protagonist of one section of this work first realizes that he is handsome when he looks in a hotel-room mirror, which leads to the realization that his $3.75 per week salary is alienating him in Washington DC. That section of this work ends with the protagonist Santosh fretting over Priya's suggest that he marry a black woman to gain citizenship. In the second section of this work, the narrator loses his money on a curry shop after he pays for Dayo's education in London. The title story of this work ends with Luke laughing mercilessly after the protagonist is beaten by the government he serves. In addition to the stories "One Out of Many" and "Tell Me Who to Kill," the title story of this work sees a gay man named Bobby take a long car trip with Linda through the fictional nation of the Southern Collectorate. For 10 points, name this work consisting of three short stories, a Booker-winner by V.S. Naipaul.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for hemoglobin oxygen binding. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diffusion-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diffusion is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in hemoglobin oxygen binding.

tossups.text: This man predicted World War I to the month, an event he tried to prevent until Kaiser Wilhelm II fired him because of his anti-Socialist domestic policy. He modified the Ems Telegram and called for the Berlin Conference. This German instigated the Seven Weeks War against Austria and the Franco-Prussian War, and was an ardent follower of Realpolitik. This man said that the failure of 1848 can only be fixed through "blood and iron" in a speech delivered to the Reichstag. For 10 points, name this "Iron Chancellor", who united Germany.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for muscle fiber types. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this sarcomere-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The sarcomere is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in muscle fiber types.

tossups.text: This ruler had to surrender most of the territory he won during one war by the terms of the Treaty of Oliva, and after reconquering it, he would later lose that same territory again at the Treaty of Saint-Germaine-en-Laye. Many of this ruler's policies, especially with regard to agriculture, were strongly influenced by the time he spent at the court of Frederick Henry of Orange, whose daughter Louise Henriette he married. This ruler attempted to maintain neutrality during the First Northern War between Sweden and Poland, but after his territories were occupied by Swedish armies under Charles X Gustav, he was forced to lead his army at the Battle of Warsaw, where his performance earned him territorial concessions to remain a Swedish ally. This ruler remained allied to Louis XIV until it became clear that Louis would not help him win Pomerania, at which point this man joined the Grand Alliance. It was with a victory over the Swedes in 1675 that this ruler gained his famous sobriquet. For 10 points, identify this father of Frederick I who consolidated the Prussian state during his rule from 1640 to 1688.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on “Frederick William” but do not accept
prompt on “Frederick William” followed by any number
The Frederick William, the Great Elector

tossups.text: One of these creatures gave birth to a grain of wheat and a bee, a grain of barley and a bee, a wolf, an eagle, and Palug's Cat. Lleuelys advised Llud on using a vat of mead and a sheet of silk to capture two dragons in this form, and Math battled Pryderi for some of these animals. One immortal took this form after being banished for flirting with the moon goddess Chang-O, and later became a guardian of the monk Xuanzong. Vishnu assumed this form to kill the demon Hiranyaksha, and Brokk and Eitri created one from gold for Frey. Henwen, Zhu Bajie ["joo ba-jyeh"], Varaha and Gullinbursti are all examples of, For 10 points, these animals, one of which was killed by Meleager during a hunt in Calydon.

Repackaging a security named for this concept forms its "squared" or "synthetic" version. That security named for this concept is divided up into "tranches" by seniority, which dictates the order in which payouts are given. A type of security widely blamed for the 2008 financial crisis was known as a "collateralized [this concept] obligation" or CDO. Firms that finance themselves in this fashion are called "levered," and the ratio of this quantity to equity is known as leverage. The ratio of a form of this quantity to GDP is projected to reach 100% by 2028; the value of that "national" type of this state is currently 21.97 trillion dollars. For 10 points, name this state of owing money.

In a story by this author, Laura torments her friend Amanda after being reincarnated as an otter. A boy created by this author decides that a Houdan hen is an Anabaptist, which he thinks is "dashing and not very respectable," and says another animal has "red thoughts and his teeth were white." A party decides to kill a cat who knows their secrets after it learns to talk in this author's story "Tobermory." In a story by this man, Vera tells her family that Mr. Nuttel was hunted in the Ganges by a "pack of pariah dogs" to create "Romance at short notice." The sickly boy Conradin prays for a ferret to kill Mrs. de Ropp in a story by this author. For 10 points, name this author of "The Open Window" and "Sredni Vashtar."

At the end of this event, women cut off a single lock of hair, and it is followed by the slaughter of an animal for the Feast of Sacrifice. At the outset of this event, men don two sheets of white and it includes drinking water from the Well of Zamzam. Participants of this event stay on Mount Arafat and indulge in "Stoning the Devil" in Mina, and an important part of this event is walking seven times around the Kaaba in a certain Arabian city. For 10 points, name this pillar of Islam that requires adherents to pilgrimage to Mecca.

Gabriel Marcel wrote a book on his "metaphysics" that focused on this man's treatment of "the one and the many." In an essay of the same name this man argued for "The Possibility of Error," which would imply the actuality of "an infinite unity of conscious thought." Other works include his literary criticism collected in the volume Fugitive Essays and a novel, The Feud of Oakfield Creek. His two-part Gifford lecture, consisting of "The Four Historical Conceptions of Being" and "Nature, Man, and the Moral Order," was published as The World and the Individual and other works composed while he was at Harvard include The Concept of God and The Spirit of Modern Philosophy. FTP identify this idealistic thinker best known for his theory of the Absolute which he promoted in his masterwork, The Religious Aspect of Philosophy.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for blood plasma. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in blood plasma.

tossups.text: According to this philosophy, air and fire form the life force pneuma. People associated with it include Chrysippus and Seneca, and according to it, divine logos is everywhere. The path to happiness according to it involves ignoring the unchangeable and Marcus Aurelius wrote about it in his Meditations. For 10 points, this is what philosophy founded by Zeno of Citium that yields a present day word meaning unaffected by emotion.

This condition is characterized by an increase in PDGF ["P-D-G-F"] and loss of E-cadherin. Knudsen's two hit hypothesis associates one type of this disease with loss of heterozygosity and mutation in Rb ["R-B"]. Li-Fraumeni syndrome greatly increases the chance of this condition because of a mutation in the p53 gene. A triple negative form of this condition lacks estrogen, progesterone, and HER2 ["HER-two"] receptors. Mutations in genes controlling apoptosis are present in this condition, which causes the spread of cells via lymphatics or blood in metastasis. For 10 points, name this disease characterized by malicious tumors.

One of his works describes how the wau and the laua interact in such ways as cutting down palm trees, and thus make up the latmul system. He collaborated on a "photographic study" of body language among the title people in one work, and he responded to Durkheim's contrast of the sacred and profane in a posthumous publication. In addition to Balinese Character and Angel's Fear, he wrote an essay on alcoholism from a cybernetic point of view in his essay collection States to an Ecology of Mind, while another work attempted to reconcile Radcliffe-Brown with Benedict in observing a New Guinea tribe from "three points of view." The author of Mind and Nature, for 10 points, name this author of Naven, the first husband of Margaret Mead.

The use of the term "anarambha" in Ashoka's Rock Edict Number 4 is analogous to this later practice, as is the Pali term "panatipata veramani." The eighth-century BCE sage Parsvanatha's used this term for prohibition of ritual slaughter, while the image of a hand with a wheel inscribed upon it with this word written in the wheel's center is a visual representation of the vow to adhere to this principle in the faith which defines it most comprehensively. Seen in action when adherents sweep their path to remove insects or other small creatures, For 10 points what is this principle most associated with Jainism, the insistence on not harming any living thing?

A nearly two hundred year old lighthouse in this body of water is built on a sandstone reef known as Bell Rock. A large shoal in this body of water became the site of an international incident after Admiral Rozhestvensky mistook fishing trawlers for Japanese torpedo boats. The western terminus of the Kiel Canal lies on this body of water. Zuiderzee, a shallow bay of this sea, was reclaimed to form IJsselmeer, a large freshwater lake. Skaggerak separates this body of water from the Kattegat, which together connect it to the Baltic Sea. This body of water contains the Frisian, Orkney, and Shetland islands. For 10 points, identify this sea separated from the English Channel by the Strait of Dover and located to the east of Great Britain.

Along with a piano concerto, a concert aria, and his Choral Fantasy, excerpts from Beethoven's C major first work in this genre were performed at the premiere of his 5th and 6th symphonies. Mozart's unfinished final work in this genre, his 17th, opens with the slow eighth notes "C slur down to staccato G-G-G, G slur down to staccato E-flat E-flat E-flat." It's not a piano concerto, but a Mozart work in this genre is nicknamed for its use at coronations. Mozart's 17th work in this genre is called the "Great" one in C minor. A late Beethoven composition named for the Solemnis subtype of this musical genre features extensive fugues in its Gloria and Credo sections. For 10 points, name these musical settings of the liturgical Ordinary that often feature a Kyrie and Agnus Dei, including Bach's one in B minor.
acceptableAnswers: accept Great Mass in C minor

tossups.text: The Cerro de las Chivas is located immediately west of this coastal city. The full name of this city's mission church refers to a local re-burial tradition involving painting the bones of the deceased with red ochre, and ends with a native word meaning "place full of reeds." Native peoples, who practiced those Las Palmas funerary rites, knew this city as Añuití, and were proselytized by Padre Nica Tamaral, who founded a church on the Plaza Mijares, but was martyred there at the beginning of the Pericú Rebellion. The reeds referred to by this city's original inhabitants referred to an estuary terminating at this oasis of the Sarcocaule Desert that is its nation's third largest, its now underground river meeting the sea at the bay of San Bernabé after beginning in the Laguna Mountains, and in the days of Vizcaino was the last source of freshwater for northbound ships before turning west toward the Philippines. This city makes up the eastern end of a touristic corridor that begins at a rock formation known as El Arco. FTP, name this southernmost of the Jesuit mission cities of Baja California that now defines a large resort corridor along with San Lucas known as Los Cabos.

The Judges of the Dead decided whether souls were to enter Hades or this location, a pit below the Earth, reserved for the most evil monsters and men. Sisyphus cheated death by trapping Thanatos in this place.
This place is reserved for righteous mortals, and is more pleasant than Asphodel. Hesiod called this place "The Isle of the Blessed."

A vignette from Tokarczuk's Flights about the Muslim woman Jasmine instructs the "citizens of the world" to perform this action. Boris Pasternak's "Black Spring" orders the reader to perform this action and "weep."

parts.text: This structure marked the northern boundary of Roman Britain. It stretches across northern England and is named for the emperor who built it.
The Celtic queen Boudica started a revolt against the Romans in this modern-day constituent country of the UK. This country to the west of England has a flag depicting a red dragon.

A modern-day English city is named for one of these structures, which the Romans built there. Visitors to these places, which the Romans called thermae, might have left their clothes in an apodyterium before using them.

parts.text: Identify this commodity that George Orwell devised 11 golden rules for making a "nice cup of." The British East India company started growing this product in Assam, and it was the subject of a certain party in Boston Harbor.

To satisfy their craving for tea, the British had to trade for tea with this Chinese guild that, by order of the Qianlong Emperor, controlled a monopoly on imports and exports as part of the Canton system.

The Canton system was set up in response to the complaints of merchant James Flint, who was jailed in Macau for 3 years. Flint's other claim to fame is that he introduced this legume to the American colonies. Henry Ford's "hemp body car" was alternatively named for this crop.

parts.text: After the death of Solomon, this son of his inherited the throne. His tax levies angered the populace.
Rehoboam was the son of this Ammonite woman, the only wife of Solomon to be mentioned by name in the bible. Her name means "pleasant."
During the reign of Rehoboam, Judah was sacked by this Egyptian Pharaoh. This event is depicted on a relief at the Bubastis Portal at Karnak.

parts.text: Name this theory described in an article by James Wilson and George Kelling. It argues that reducing the rate of smaller crimes in urban areas will reduce the rate of bigger crimes.
Broken windows theory argues that more serious crimes will be curbed by reducing this specific criminal act of damaging property, which includes things like graffiti.
In his book The Tipping Point, this author argues that the use of broken windows theory in New York City has reduced crime. His latest book is David and Goliath.

bonuses.leadin: Philip Zimbardo tested this theory by placing an automobile without a license plate in the middle of Palo Alto, California. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this year in which an inebriated Union general "sadly...unbuckled his sword" in surrender in the alternate history story "If Grant Had Been Drinking at Appomattox."

This author wrote "If Grant Had Been Drinking at Appomattox." Mr. Martin pretends to be "coked to the gills" during a fake murder plot to get Mrs. Barrows fired in this author's story "The Catbird Seat."

This Brit wrote the oddly-titled alternate history story "If Lee Had NOT Won the Battle of Gettysburg." He won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Literature for "brilliant oratory" and works like A History of the English-Speaking Peoples.

parts.text: Name this holiday that occurs on the first of Tishrei, ten days before Yom Kippur. This first of the High Holy Days commemorates the Jewish New Year.
During Rash Hashanah, participants eat apples dipped in this substance. In Exodus, God tells the Israelites that the promised land is flowing with milk and this other substance.
If Rosh Hashanah falls on this day, the shofar, a trumpet made out of a ram's horn, is not blown. On this day, wine is blessed with the kiddush before an evening ceremony that ushers in the new week.

This colleague of Cornelius Jansen encouraged Jansen to publish the Augustinus. A teacher of Arnauld, he spent several years in prison at the orders of Cardinal Richelieu.

This doubly-eponymous American Indian language family is rich in affricate. It includes the Athabascan languages and Tlingit. Most members of this family are found in Alaska or Canada.

The Na-Dene language with the most speakers is this one, spoken in the American southwest. Speakers of this language were famously used as "code-talkers" during World War II, because the Japanese could not understand this language.

parts.text: Another Jewish theological explanation for the Holocaust comes from this seventh Lubavitch Hasidic Rebbe, who controversially analogized the Holocaust to a surgery, but also said that it could not be rationally explained.

Emil Fackenheim described the 614th one of these statements as instructing Jews not to give in to Hitler. Judaism normally considers there to be 613 of these statements, including a set of 10 given to Moses on Sinai.

Reports that no one who sold this product had died of the plague led to its widespread use as a prophylactic. Murad IV and Michael Romanov both instituted death penalties for consumption of this good.
Following the subsequent Great Fire of London, this surveyor supervised the rebuilding of the city. This man included images of a gnat and a louse in his text, Micrographia.

parts.text: Barkley was a fur trader who worked with the chief Maquinna on this island, which shares its name with a small body of water that was the subject of a dispute between Spain, Britain and the US in the Pacific Northwest.

Barkley hired the servant Wynee in this archipelago, making her the first native of this place to travel abroad on a European ship. Shortly after Barkley's visit, Kamehameha the Great unified this archipelago.

Barkley's wife Frances was the first woman to openly circumnavigate the globe, though she was preceded by this French woman in disguise, who joined her likely lover Philibert Commerson on the Bougainville expedition.
